subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should shipped legacy session rows with no `pluginOwnerId` remain unpatchable by every plugin-runtime caller, or must OpenClaw provide a safe ownership migration or temporary compatibility path?
rationale: Fail-closed is the strongest isolation rule and matches the existing delete fence, but it changes a shipped persisted-state workflow and no maintainer has confirmed the upgrade policy.

options.title: Approve fail-closed
options.body: Reject all ownerless rows for plugin-runtime patch calls and document the operator or non-plugin recovery path.

options.title: Migrate known ownership
options.body: Add a narrow doctor or plugin-owned migration when ownership can be established safely before runtime enforcement.

options.title: Temporary compatibility
options.body: Preserve limited ownerless access with an explicit deprecation and removal plan, accepting weaker cross-plugin isolation.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed
recommendation.body: Reject all ownerless rows for plugin-runtime patch calls and document the operator or non-plugin recovery path.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the session-management behavior and is the strongest history-backed owner for the security and upgrade boundary.
